Thanks Soojin — digging in now. Quick summary of what we're seeing from platform telemetry (prelim):

- Concurrency and backlog: Bluehaven's tenant concurrency cap is set to 32. At 08:10 PST we observe bursts that push active concurrency to that cap; queue depth climbs and head-of-line requests block downstream batching.
- Cache coldness + prefix miss: KV/prefix cache hit-rate drops sharply at the start of the window (many short-lived keys). That increases per-request work (KV fetch + model KV misses), amplifying latency.
- Staggered execution / misaligned arrival: Their client pattern shows many small groups arriving with inter-request gaps of 10-50ms. This misalignment prevents the runtime from forming efficient continuous batches and instead creates many tiny micro-batches that increase per-token latency. I labeled this "staggered execution" in the traces.
- Error surface: 503s correlate with transient local executor overload where the queue spikes beyond per-executor queue-length limit and triggers a fast-fail.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (fast):
1) Bump Bluehaven per-tenant concurrency cap from 32 -> 64 for a 2-hour window (manual override) — low risk, buys throughput headroom.
2) Enable emergency prefix cache warming for their tenant (seed top prefixes from recent traffic) — reduces cold-miss amplification.
3) Route traffic heavier than 400 tokens to redwood-small-v2 (lower memory path) for the next 90 minutes to reduce KV pressure; this reduces model quality slightly but lowers per-request work.
4) Temporarily relax the executor queue-length fast-fail threshold for their shard from 128->192 (reduce 503s while we scale).

I'll run a targeted runbook: collect p50/p95/p99 before/after changes, keep logs. ETA for executing the changes: ~18 minutes if we get approval.

Attachments: cpu_profile_0327.svg (sample CPU profile showing spikes during backlog)

If Soojin approves, I'll enact 1-3 and monitor.
